title: May nitrate load share gave no clear period change at two Gulf river outlets in 1980–2025
abstract: We tested whether May nitrate delivery changed in step with annual delivery at the Mississippi and Atchafalaya outlets. We used archived daily USGS Kalman load estimates and compared 1980–1996 with 2009–2025. The combined May share rose from 13.437% to 13.720%, a change of 0.283 percentage points. A conditional 95% three-year block interval was −1.676 to +2.651 points. Separate river, wider spring-window and alternative-period tests also gave intervals that included zero. Stationary flow normalization gave a negative point change, while generalized normalization gave little change. These comparisons do not isolate a flow effect. Daily Kalman sums differ from the annual source table by up to 1.55%; exact annual rescaling changes the main contrast to 0.278 points. The evidence does not resolve a shift in May delivery share. Year resampling does not include USGS source-model uncertainty. The study does not test hypoxia or biological recovery. Code, monthly evidence, source hashes, audit results and a figure permit reproduction.

display.caption: May shares and changes between 1980–1996 and 2009–2025. Bars are conditional year-block intervals, not USGS model-error intervals.
